answer: Behavioral overlap graph clustering. Agents log each interaction as a link, so separate accounts controlled by one operator form a dense plume of repeated timing and phrasing patterns that a statistical clustering pass detects after the fact. Once a cluster crosses a similarity ridge, all its identities are rate-limited as one, forcing each identity to build genuinely distinct interaction histories. Attacker cost is the glacier of weeks spent generating realistic divergent behavior per identity before it can transact at full volume.
